* [[Ken Mehlman]] is to step down as chairman of the [[Republican National Committee|National Committee]] of the [[United States]] [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican Party]]. [http://edition.cnn.com/2006/POLITICS/11/09/mehlman.steppingdown/index.html (CNN)]
* Eight synchronized bombs hit car showrooms in Southern [[Thailand]], nine injured. [https://www.nytimes.com/reuters/world/international-security-thailand.html (Reuters)]{{Dead link|date=August 2021 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}
* [[President of Kyrgyzstan|Kyrgyz President]] [[Kurmanbek Bakiyev]] formally signs the new [[Constitution of Kyrgyzstan]]. The Constitution drastically weakens the power of the [[executive branch]] in favor of the [[legislative branch|legislative]]. Bakiyev and [[Prime Minister of Kyrgyzstan|Prime Minister]] [[Felix Kulov]] are expected to maintain their positions until 2010. [https://web.archive.org/web/20070607003121/http://www.eurasianet.org/departments/insight/articles/eav110906.shtml (EurasiaNet)]
* [[2006 United States elections]]: 
** [[2006 United States Senate elections]]:
*** [[List of United States senators from Montana|Montana Senator]] [[Conrad Burns]] concedes his [[United States Senate|U.S. Senate]] [[2006 United States Senate election in Montana|race]] to [[Jon Tester]]. [https://news.yahoo.com/s/ap/20061109/ap_on_el_se/montana_senate_12 (AP via Yahoo! News)]
*** [[List of United States senators from Virginia|Virginia Senator]] [[George Allen (American politician)|George Allen]] to concede his [[2006 United States Senate election in Virginia|U.S. Senate race]] to [[Jim Webb|James Webb]]. This gives control of the U.S. Senate to the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrats]]. [https://news.yahoo.com/s/ap/20061109/ap_on_el_se/virginia_senate (AP via Yahoo! News)]
** A recount is reported to be underway in [[Florida's 13th congressional district]], after [[Christine Jennings]], who lost her bid for [[Katherine Harris]]'s former House seat by 373 votes, alleges that touch-screen voter machine malfunctions failed to record 18,000 votes in [[Sarasota County, Florida]], a Jennings stronghold. [https://news.yahoo.com/s/ap/20061109/ap_on_el_ho/florida_recount (AP via Yahoo! News)]
* [[BP]] settles the last remaining lawsuit from the 2005 explosion at its [[Texas]] [[oil refinery]] that cost 15 lives. [http://www.iii.co.uk/news/?type=reutersnews&articleid=MTFH54474_2006-11-09_17-18-05_N09409672&feed=Bus&action=article (Reuters via Interactive Investor)]
* The [[Bank of England]] raises [[interest rate]]s in the [[United Kingdom]] to five percent. [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/main.jhtml?xml=/news/2006/11/09/uboe109.xml (Daily Telegraph)]{{Dead link|date=August 2021 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}
* [[Israel]] braces itself for revenge attacks after yesterday's dawn barrage in the [[Gaza Strip]] leaves a family of 18 dead. The general in charge of Israel's Southern Command, Youav Galant, blames problems with the targeting device for the [[artillery]] strike. * Dr [[Mahathir Mohamad]], the former [[Prime Minister of Malaysia]], is hospitalized following a [[myocardial infarction|heart attack]]. [http://edition.cnn.com/2006/WORLD/asiapcf/11/08/mahathir.heart.ap/ (CNN)]
* [[France]] successfully performs the first flight test of its new nuclear missile, the [[M51 SLBM|M51]]. [http://www.cbsnews.com/stories/2006/11/09/ap/world/mainD8L9JUP00.shtml (AP via CBS)]
* Hundreds of young [[United Kingdom|British]] [[Muslims]] are being radicalised, groomed and set on a path to [[mass murder]], according to the head of [[MI5|MI5 (Security Service)]], [[Dame (title)|Dame]] [[Eliza Manningham-Buller]].
